entities.summary: Fort Dansborg, locally called Danish Fort, is a Danish fort located in the shores of Bay of Bengal in Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) in the Mayiladuthurai District, state of Tamil Nadu. Fort Dansborg was built in the land ceded by Thanjavur king Ragunatha Nayak in an agreement with Danish Admiral Ove Gjedde in 1620 and acted as the base for Danish settlement in the region during the early 17th century. The fort is the second largest Danish fort after Kronborg. The fort was sold to the British in 1845 and along with Tranquebar, the fort lost its significance as the town was not an active trading post for the British.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fort Dansborg played a significant role in establishing Danish settlement in South Asia during the early 17th century. Although it was sold to the British in 1845 and lost its importance as a trading post, its legacy remains as a testament to Denmark's colonial presence in the region.
